match.reason: The bank point chem-covalent-bonding is Year 11 depth, covering molecular and network solids, melting points and why covalent substances do not conduct like ions, which goes well beyond the short Stage 5 brief about non-metal atoms sharing electrons to form molecules like water and O2.

draft.title: Covalent bonding
card: A covalent bond forms when two atoms share a pair of electrons. It usually forms between non-metal atoms.
Sharing lets each atom fill its outer shell, so the atoms end up more stable than they were apart. No electrons are fully transferred, so no ions form.
A group of atoms joined by covalent bonds is a molecule. Water, H2O, is a molecule: one oxygen atom shares electrons with two hydrogen atoms.
Some elements also exist as molecules. Oxygen is found as O2, a pair of oxygen atoms sharing electrons.
draft.remember: Covalent bonds are shared electrons, usually between non-metal atoms, and they make molecules.

a.q: What happens to electrons when a covalent bond forms between two atoms?
opts: The atoms share a pair of electrons
One atom gives electrons to the other
The electrons are lost from both atoms
The electrons move freely between many atoms
a.why: In a covalent bond, two atoms share electrons so each can fill its outer shell. Giving electrons from one atom to another is what happens when ions form, and that is not covalent bonding.

b.q: Which of these is made of molecules held together by covalent bonds?
opts: Oxygen gas, O2
A piece of copper wire
Sodium chloride, NaCl
A lump of solid sodium metal
b.why: Oxygen gas is made of pairs of non-metal atoms sharing electrons, so each O2 is a molecule. Sodium chloride is tempting because it contains a non-metal, but it is a metal joined to a non-metal, which forms ions rather than shared pairs.
b.clue: Look for atoms of non-metals only.

wants.brief: A water molecule, H2O, showing one oxygen atom in the centre joined to two hydrogen atoms. Each bond is drawn as a shared pair of electrons between the oxygen atom and a hydrogen atom. Label the oxygen atom, the two hydrogen atoms and a shared pair of electrons.
wants.why: Seeing the shared pairs between atoms shows how a molecule is held together.

a.best: The atoms share a pair of electrons
